why: Vendored, not fetched. prophet-platform (SocioProphet) and sourceos-spec (SourceOS-Linux) are in different orgs, so CI's GITHUB_TOKEN cannot read the spec: a cross-repo checkout fails and the conformance job can only report UNVERIFIED. A gate that depends on network access it does not have is not a gate. So the vectors are vendored with their upstream digests recorded here, and the conformance tests run against the vendored copy unconditionally — they can never skip. When the real spec IS present (a dev tree, or CI with cross-org access) the tests ADDITIONALLY assert the vendored copy still matches these digests, which is what catches drift. Never-skipping conformance, plus drift detection wherever it is actually possible.
